A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MLLM-For3D, and their text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends with references despite mentioning supplementary material; v2 includes readable Appendices A and B.

before.justification: v1 reports original MLLM-For3D evaluations on Instruct3D, Intent3D, and VG-w/o-ON, including component ablations and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and adds Reason3D results, view-selection experiments, and the comparisons in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 revise central fusion and training procedures. v1 averages query tokens and uses confidence-weighted exponential similarities; v2 describes attention-weighted query fusion, clipped dot-product weights, and low-confidence/small-mask filtering. Its BCE query-to-point supervision and cosine 2D–3D feature-consistency objective also differ substantively from v1's feature-attention and prediction-consensus formulation.

E1.justification: v2 adds Reason3D query-conditioned segmentation evaluations on ScanNetV2 and Matterport3D, extending both query/mask coverage and the represented indoor environments. The existing Instruct3D, Intent3D, and VG-w/o-ON evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the reasoning-segmentation comparators with 3D-STMN and zero-shot/fine-tuned rows labeled Intent3D. The Instruct3D row attributed to LLM-Grounder in v1 is attributed to SegPoint in v2, retaining 23.7/15.6/17.2. Appendix B additionally reports explicit ChatScene+Mask3D comparisons under fine-tuned and zero-shot settings.

E3.justification: Reason3D and MLLM-For3D Intent3D scores move from AP@0.25/0.50 in v1 Table 3 to Acc@0.25/0.50 in v2 Table 2. This is a substantive reported metric revision, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Added experiments introduce official Reason3D splits, 2/4/8-view settings, and fine-tuned/zero-shot ChatScene+Mask3D evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: v2 Table 4 and Section 4.3 extend the existing component/backbone analyses with a focused 2-, 4-, and 8-view sensitivity study and robustness checks across random four-view selections. These test how view quantity and sampling affect supervision and segmentation; the original qualitative comparison cases are largely retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports no repeated-trial uncertainty estimates. v2 Section 4.3 reports five random four-view configurations, yielding Acc@0.25 39.10±0.61, Acc@0.50 29.70±0.48, and mIoU 23.90±0.52. The meaning of ± is unspecified, and these trials do not establish repeated training with different seeds.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial Reason3D, view-count, and Appendix B results; for example, label-free VideoLISA reports 44.18/34.80/32.90 for accuracy at 0.25/0.50 and mIoU on Reason3D ScanNet. Shared Instruct3D and VG-w/o-ON main-table values remain unchanged. Table 4 reassigns retained single-module scores to opposite ablations and changes its left-hand benchmark label from Intent3D to Instruct3D. Intent3D metric reassignment does not demonstrate a performance gain.

T1.justification: The central mathematical formulation changes from v1's exponential attention and per-point feature-fusion definitions to clipped-similarity weighting and explicit BCE semantic-alignment, cosine feature-consistency, and combined-loss definitions in v2 Equations 1–3. These are substantive changes to mathematical definitions, beyond notation or equation numbering. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The principal claims of label-free transfer, spatial consistency, token-for-query alignment, and strong segmentation performance remain. v2's abstract additionally presents token-attention filtering of irrelevant views as an explicit step addressing hallucinated predictions, modestly extending the stated contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explains the four-view accuracy/cost tradeoff through missing objects with sparse views and conflicting signals with additional views. It removes v1's attribution of VideoLISA gains to temporal context; Appendix A.3 specifies single-frame operation without temporal aggregation. Appendix B adds data-scarcity and hallucination explanations for comparator failures, while the general computational-cost limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix A supplies implementation information absent from the supplied v1: MinkowskiNet14 architecture, optimizer and augmentation details, dataset-specific learning rates and batch sizes, 40-epoch training, voxel size, four A100 GPUs, and training times. v2 also clarifies frozen/single-frame 2D-model usage and provides a code-availability link. These are principally new disclosures, not evidence that every setting changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantive discussion of Point-Bind/Point-LLM and LERF, alongside new multiview-method and comparator citations. Several earlier zero-shot references and LLM-Grounder are removed. The central positioning as label-free transfer from 2D models, contrasted with supervised 3D alignment or fine-tuning, remains.

P1.justification: Section 3 is extensively rewritten from four component-focused subsections into three organized around pseudo-label generation, training, and inference. Semantic/spatial explanations and ablation ordering change, Intent3D and VG-w/o-ON discussions are reordered, and Appendices A/B establish a separate technical and additional-comparison structure.

P2.justification: The two-column presentation becomes a single-column NeurIPS layout. v1's opening teaser figure is removed, its architecture diagram is substantially redrawn, and retained qualitative examples gain success/failure markers. Table 1 becomes a three-dataset comparison, Table 4 gains view configurations and colored differences, and new configuration and appendix comparison tables are added.

improvement.justification: The added training recipe, explicit objectives, and view-selection checks address real omissions in v1. However, v2 Table 2 relabels retained Intent3D scores as accuracy while Section 4.1 still claims AP gains against IntentNet. Table 4 also assigns unchanged scores to opposite component ablations without explanation. These unresolved changes affect core comparisons and component attribution, preventing a confident net quality judgment despite substantially fuller documentation.
